title: Immutable admin activity guardrail + residency-aware retention automation
creator: Marina Chen
description:
Objective: Build an automated orchestration layer that enforces immutable admin action logging (WORM semantics) across residency zones, applies per-tenant retention profiles, and emits signed evidence bundles for regulatory reporting. Scope includes admin actions (console/API), config changes, access grants, and retention lifecycle events (rollover, purge, legal hold).

Acceptance criteria:
- All admin actions for tenants with residency constraints are captured to an append-only store with S3 Object Lock or equivalent WORM backend per-region.
- Retention policies are enforced automatically by policy engine; purge operations are gated by signed manifests and legal-hold checks.
- Evidence export endpoint can produce a compressed, signed bundle with manifest and sha256 checksums for a given timespan and residency zone.
- Automated integrity verification job runs and reports checksum drift; any mismatch creates a high-sev alert and a read-only snapshot of implicated objects.

Technical design summary:
- Ingest: router emits admin-event protobuf to regional collector; collector writes both to local append-only store and replicates metadata to the global audit-index (searchable, read-only).
- WORM path: use S3 Object Lock + bucket-level retention for cloud regions; for on-prem/VPC use local immutable store shim (write-once filesystem + signed object manifests).
- Evidence bundling: background exporter composes bundles with manifest.json (entries: object_key, sha256, size, timestamp, signer_id). Each bundle is signed with KMS-backed key (customer-specific when required).
- Verification: periodic verifier recomputes sha256 and compares to manifest; verifier writes verification-result objects (signed) and emits alerts if >0 mismatches.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Chose S3 Object Lock for hosted customers to leverage native WORM and lifecycle; on-prem needs a shim which increases surface area and testing burden.
- Replication: full object replication avoided to reduce cross-region transfer costs; instead we replicate immutable metadata and store cryptographic anchors (merkle root) per-day to a long-lived anchor store.
- Retention enforcement is policy-driven but purge operations remain an operator-only flow protected by multi-sig approval for P0 customers.

Progress updates:
- 2025-02-21: Initial design doc created and shared. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMPLIANCE/Immutable+Admin+Audit+Guardrail
- 2025-02-25: Spike completed to validate S3 Object Lock semantics across our infra accounts; findings: Object Lock requires versioning + correct retention mode; latency for retention changes is eventually consistent. See spike notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/spikes/ENG-43100-s3-lock-spike.md
- 2025-02-28: Prototype exporter implemented (region-us) and PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12987
- 2025-03-03: Security review kickoff; identified KMS key access patterns and need for HSM-backed signing for enterprise.

Review feedback (from PM/Design/Security):
- PM (Vikram): require per-tenant audit visibility in Console with read-only manifests and download controls.
- Security (Nadia): require rotation policy for signing keys and an audit trail of key usage.
- Design (Asha): Console export UX needs a progress indicator and clear residency label.
Action items from reviews: add key-usage logs, add export progress flow in console, add customer opt-in for anchored notarization.

Rollout plan:
- Canary regional rollout (us-east-1) for internal + 2 beta customers (late March).
- Monitor checksum mismatch rate, export latency, evidence bundle size, and retention enforcement errors. SLOs: zero silent purges; <1% bundle export failures; checksum mismatch alerts must be fired within 5 minutes.

Operational playbook (short):
- On verification mismatch: open incident -> snapshot implicated objects -> run reingest verifier -> escalate to security + legal.
- On failed export: automatic retry x3, then escalate to on-call.

Open questions / blockers:
- Finalize on-prem WORM shim API (storage team dependency).
- Legal hold semantics for cross-residency data when customer spans multiple regions.
- Pricing/metric for evidence export bandwidth and storage.

Next steps:
- Finish on-prem shim prototype (storage team).
- Implement key-usage logging + rotation hooks (security).
- Build Console export UX wireframes and link to exporter backend (design + frontend).
